title: One formula for every prompt

sources.name: Prompting guidance: clear instructions, context and output format

caption:
One simple formula you can reuse for almost any prompt: task, context, format and limits.
Swap in your own details, then review the draft before you use it.
Save this template. Comment FORMULA and I will send it.

slides.headline: Four parts, every time
body: Context: what it needs to know.
Format and limits: how the answer looks.

slides.headline: Start with the task
body: Use a clear verb: draft, compare, summarize, list.
slides.prompt: Summarize the article below for a busy manager.

slides.headline: Add the context
body: Include the audience, the goal and anything it cannot guess.
slides.prompt: The reader has two minutes and needs to decide whether to attend the event. My goal is a clear yes or no.

slides.headline: Choose the format
body: Ask for bullets, a table or numbered steps.
slides.prompt: Use three bullet points: what it is, why it matters and what to do next.

slides.headline: Set the limits
body: Length, tone and things to avoid.
slides.prompt: Stay under 80 words. Use plain language and avoid jargon.

slides.headline: The full prompt
body: Copy this and swap in your own details.
slides.prompt: Summarize [article] for a busy manager deciding whether to attend [event]. Use three bullets: what it is, why it matters, what to do next. Under 80 words, plain language.

slides.headline: Fix one thing at a time
body: Ask for a single change instead of starting over.
slides.prompt: Keep the same bullets, but make the tone more direct and add one risk to consider.

slides.headline: You review the result
body: Names, dates and numbers need your eyes.
Treat uncertain claims as things to verify.

slides.headline: Save the four-part formula
body: Comment FORMULA and I will send the template.
Share this with someone who types one-line prompts.
